title: The Black Death (1348) and the Poisoned Well Myth
hero_object: Papal Bull of Clement VI (Avignon, 1348) Sicut Judaeis
hook: The accusation spread. That didn’t make it evidence.
punchline: A thousand people repeating it is still not a source.
visual_paradigm: Medieval Illuminated Manuscript & Papal Decree (Vellum Sepia #FEF3C7, Crimson Wax #991B1B, Iron Gall Ink #1F2937)

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: The accusation spread. That didn’t make it evidence.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: In thirteen-forty-eight, the Black Death swept across Europe. Terrified communities, lacking germ theory, looked for someone to blame.
scenes.on_screen: 1348 BLACK DEATH: CRISIS WITHOUT GERM THEORY

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: The rumor spread that local Jewish families were poisoning village wells. Mobs attacked communities, extracting false confessions through torture.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Even at the time, perceptive leaders saw through it. Pope Clement the Sixth issued two papal bulls in thirteen-forty-eight condemning the accusation as a lie.
scenes.on_screen: POPE CLEMENT VI: CONDEMNED ACCUSATION IN 1348

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: He pointed out the obvious logic: Jewish people were dying of the plague at the exact same rates, and in places where no Jewish communities existed, the plague raged just as hard.
scenes.on_screen: IDENTICAL PLAGUE RATES REVEALED THE LIE

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: When fear replaces investigation, scapegoats replace science. Repetition by a frightened crowd never turns a myth into fact.
scenes.on_screen: FEAR REPLACES SCIENCE · MOB RUMORS ≠ FACTS

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: A thousand people repeating it is still not a source.
scenes.on_screen: A THOUSAND PEOPLE REPEATING IT IS NOT A SOURCE
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
